text: The Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions has released a revised Guideline B-13 on Technology and Cyber Risk Management. The revised guideline strengthens expectations for incident reporting, requiring federally regulated financial institutions to report technology and cyber incidents promptly. It introduces enhanced requirements for third-party technology risk management across the provider lifecycle. Institutions must demonstrate board oversight of technology risk and maintain tested resilience capabilities. The guideline is effective immediately and applies to all federally regulated banks and insurers.
title: OSFI releases revised Guideline B-13 on Technology and Cyber Risk Management

text: The New York Department of Financial Services has adopted amendments to 23 NYCRR Part 500, its cybersecurity regulation. Covered entities must notify the superintendent within 72 hours of a cybersecurity event with a reasonable likelihood of material harm, and within 72 hours of making any ransomware payment. The amendments require CISOs to report material issues to the board and mandate privileged access management and endpoint detection. Compliance deadlines are phased based on company size, with the largest entities facing the earliest dates.
title: NYDFS adopts amendments to 23 NYCRR Part 500 cybersecurity regulation

text: The Securities and Exchange Commission has adopted rules requiring public companies to disclose material cybersecurity incidents. Registrants must report material incidents on Form 8-K Item 1.05 within four business days of determining materiality. The rules also require annual disclosure of cybersecurity risk management, strategy, and governance, including board oversight of cyber risk. The disclosure requirements apply to all domestic registrants and are intended to give investors consistent, decision-useful information.
title: SEC adopts cybersecurity incident disclosure rules for public companies

text: CISA has added multiple ransomware-associated vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. Federal agencies are required to remediate listed vulnerabilities by the binding operational directive deadlines. CISA strongly urges all organizations, including financial sector entities, to prioritize patching and review logging for indicators of compromise. The advisory notes active exploitation by ransomware affiliates targeting internet-facing systems.
title: CISA adds ransomware-linked vulnerabilities to Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog

text: The Financial Services Regulatory Authority of Ontario has issued guidance on operational risk management for provincially regulated insurers. The guidance sets expectations for outsourcing oversight, business continuity planning, and incident reporting to the regulator. Insurers are expected to assess the guidance against current practices and address gaps within twelve months. FSRA will consider the guidance in its supervisory examinations going forward.
title: FSRA issues operational risk management guidance for Ontario insurers

text: The National Institute of Standards and Technology has released version 2.0 of the Cybersecurity Framework. CSF 2.0 adds a sixth function, Govern, covering organizational risk management strategy and oversight. The framework expands its scope beyond critical infrastructure to all organizations and adds implementation examples and informative references. Organizations currently aligned to CSF 1.1 should map existing controls to the new function and category structure.
title: NIST releases Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 with new Govern function

text: State insurance regulators continue advancing adoption of the NAIC Insurance Data Security Model Law. The model law requires licensees to maintain a written information security program and notify the state insurance commissioner within 72 hours of a cybersecurity event affecting 250 or more consumers. Insurers operating in multiple states must track each adopting state's effective date and variations. Third-party service provider oversight requirements apply to vendors with access to nonpublic information.
title: NAIC model data security law adoption expands across states

text: The Canadian Centre for Cyber Security has issued an advisory on evolving state-sponsored threat activity targeting Canadian organizations. The advisory recommends enhanced monitoring, multi-factor authentication on all remote access, and review of incident response plans. Financial sector entities are urged to share indicators of compromise with the Centre. Organizations should validate backup and recovery procedures against ransomware scenarios.
title: Canadian Centre for Cyber Security issues advisory on state-sponsored threat activity

text: The Financial Consumer Agency of Canada has published updated expectations for complaint handling at federally regulated banks. Banks must ensure complaint procedures are accessible, acknowledge complaints promptly, and provide clear escalation paths to senior management. The Agency will assess compliance through supervisory reviews and may take enforcement action for persistent deficiencies. Banks should update internal policies and staff training within six months.
title: FCAC updates complaint-handling expectations for federal banks
